subject: general
question: The interest on a certain deposit at 3.5% per annum will be ₹210 in one year. How much will the additional interest in one year be on the same deposit at 4% per annum?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

If 3.5 = 210

⇒ 1 = 60

⇒ 4 = 4 x 60 = 240

Additional interest = 240 - 210 = Rs.30

**∴ Additional interest in one year is Rs.30**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Given:

Initial R = 3.5%

Initial interest = Rs. 210

New R = 4%

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest = (Principle × Rate per annum ×Time)/100

**Calculation:**

Let deposit = Rs. a 

⇒ 210 = (a x 3.5 x 1)/100

⇒ a = 6000

Now,

Simple interest on 4% = (6000 x 4 x 1)/100

⇒ 240

Additional interest = 240 - 210 = Rs. 30

∴ Additional interest in one year is Rs. 30

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** Simple interest = (Principle x Rate per annum x Time)/100

Amount = Simple interest + Principle
